en: The *Nāmasaṃgīti* of Non-dual Ultimate Reality. Oṃ. Homage to the glorious Mahāmañjunātha!
Now, the glorious Vajradhara, the supreme tamer of the difficult to tame—
The hero who conquers the three worlds, the king of secrets, the lord of the vajra.
His eyes are like blossomed white lotuses, his face is like a fully opened lotus,
and he repeatedly brandishes an excellent vajra with his hand.
Accompanied by infinite Vajrapāṇis, foremost among whom are those with ripples of frowning brows—
heroes who subdue the difficult to tame, possessing forms that are both heroic and loathsome.
With their own hands brandishing the tips of flashing vajras, they perform the welfare of the world through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion; they are supreme.

Together with the Protectors who perform the deeds of a Buddha, who possess joyful and contented dispositions, who are delighted, and who manifest forms of wrathful bodies while their own bodies remain bowed in prostration.
Having prostrated before the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed Tathāgata,
he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and spoke these words.
For my benefit, for my sake, and out of compassion for me, O Lord,
[teach] so that I may become an attainer of the *Māyājāla-abhisambodhi*.
For the benefit of all sentient beings sunk in the mire of ignorance and whose minds are agitated by the afflictions, and for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit.

May the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Guru of the World— supreme knower of the reality of the great commitment and master of the inclinations of the faculties— reveal [it].
Of the Bhagavat’s Wisdom-Body, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Lord of Speech,
the Wisdom-Being Mañjuśrī, the embodiment of wisdom, the Self-Arisen One.
The supreme *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which possesses profound meaning, noble meaning, and great meaning; which is peerless and auspicious; and which is virtuous in its beginning, middle, and end.
That which was spoken by the Buddhas of the past, will be spoken by those of the future,
and is spoken again and again by the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the present.
And that which is fully proclaimed in this *Māyājāla* Great Tantra by the immeasurable, joyful holders of mantra, the Great Vajradharas.
And I, with firm resolve, shall maintain this until final liberation,
so that I may become, O Lord, the upholder of the secrets of all the perfectly awakened ones.
I shall reveal [this] for the sake of sentient beings according to the distinctions of their inclinations,
for the destruction of all afflictions and for the abandonment of all ignorance.
Having thus entreated the Tathāgata, Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets,
stood before him with his body bowed and his hands joined in the gesture of reverence.
Thus end the sixteen verses on the knowledge of the request.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Perfectly Awakened One, the supreme among bipeds,
extended his long, broad, and beautiful tongue from his own mouth.
Displaying a smile that purifies the three lower realms for all beings,
illuminating the three worlds, and subduing the enemy of the four Māras.
With a sweet, Brahma-like voice that filled the three worlds,
he addressed Vajrapāṇi, the lord of secrets and possessor of great power.
Excellent, O glorious Vajradhara! Excellent to you, O Vajrapāṇi, who, endowed with great compassion, [teach] that for the sake of the welfare of the world.
You are prepared to hear from me the *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which is of great significance, purifying, and destructive of evil, belonging to Mañjuśrī, the Wisdom Body.
"Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, I shall teach this to you;
listen with a one-pointed mind. "Very well, Blessed One," he replied.
Thus end the six verses on the knowledge of the reply.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great family of mantras, the family of mantra-vidyādharas, and the three families— Mns_23.
The worldly and supramundane family, the great family that illuminates the world,
the supreme family of Mahāmudrā, and the great family of Mahoṣṇīṣa.
Thus are the two verses on the knowledge that beholds the six families.
The Lord of Speech uttered this verse, which is the union of these six kings of mantras, the arising of non-duality, and characterized by the nature of non-arising.
A, Ā, I, Ī, U, Ū, E, AI, O, AU, AṂ, AḤ— abiding in the heart,
I am the embodiment of wisdom, the awakened one among the Buddhas who exist throughout the three times.

Oṃ, homage to you, the embodiment of the wisdom-knowledge that cuts through suffering with the adamantine edge, the Lord of Speech, the body of gnosis, who brings about the pacification [of all things]. These are the three verses from the sequence of the *Māyājāla-abhisambodhi*.
Thus it is: the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*;
the syllable *A* is the foremost of all letters, of great significance, and the supreme syllable.
For it is the Great Breath, indeed non-arising, devoid of verbal expression;
it is the foremost cause of all designations and the perfect radiance of all speech.
The great festival of the great passion, who brings delight to all sentient beings;
the great festival of the great hatred, the great enemy of all afflictions.
The great festival, the great delusion, the destroyer of the delusion of the dull-witted;
the great festival, the great wrath, the great enemy of wrath, the Supreme One.
The great festival, possessing great greed, the destroyer of all greed;
the great desire, the great bliss, the great joy, and the great delight.
He has a great form, a great body, a great complexion, and a great physique;
he possesses a great name, is most noble, and has a vast and expansive mandala.
He who wields the weapon of great wisdom, the foremost hook for the great afflictions;
he of great renown, great fame, great light, and great splendor.
The wise one who possesses the great illusion, the accomplisher of the purpose of the great illusion,
he who delights in the pleasure of the great illusion, and the master of the great illusory net.
The supreme great lord of donors, the foremost upholder of great ethical discipline,
the steadfast bearer of great patience, and one whose prowess is great vigor.
Abiding in the samādhi of great meditative concentration, he is the bearer of the body of great wisdom;
he possesses great power and great skillful means, being the vow and the ocean of primordial gnosis.
Consisting of great loving-kindness, immeasurable, possessing great compassion,
of supreme intellect, of great wisdom, of great intelligence, of great skillful means, and of great action.
Endowed with the power of great supernatural faculties, possessing great speed and great velocity,
he is of great miraculous power, of great renown, and of great strength and prowess.
The shatterer of the great mountain of existence, the dense wielder of the great vajra;
the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the one who causes fear even to the fearful.
The Lord is the supreme among great vidyās, the Guru is the supreme among great mantras;
he has ascended the path of the Mahāyāna and is the highest of the Mahāyāna way.
Thus end the fourteen verses on the wisdom of the Vajradhātu-maṇḍala:
The Buddha Mahāvairocana is the Great Silent One, the Great Sage;
he has arisen from the Great Mantra Method and is the very essence of the Great Mantra Method.
He has attained the ten perfections; he is the locus of the ten perfections;
he is the purity of the ten perfections; he is the method of the ten perfections.
The Lord is the master of the ten stages, established upon the ten stages;
his self is purified by the ten knowledges, and he maintains the purity of the ten knowledges.
The Lord of Sages has ten aspects and ten objects; he is the All-Pervading One endowed with the ten powers.
He accomplishes the welfare of the entire world without exception; he is the Great One who masters the ten aspects.
Beginningless, of a nature free from conceptual proliferation, pure in essence, and having suchness as its self;
he speaks the truth, speaks according to reality, acts accordingly, and his word is never otherwise.
Non-dual and proponent of non-duality, established in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi),
he roars the lion’s roar of selflessness, terrifying the deer-like false teachers.
All-pervading, of unfailing course, with the speed of a Tathāgata’s mind;
the Victor, who has conquered his enemies, the triumphant one, the universal monarch of great power.
The leader of the host, the teacher of the host, the lord of the host, the master of the host, the self-controlled one;
the one of great majesty, the foremost bearer of the burden, the one not led by another, the one of the great way.
Lord of speech, master of speech, eloquent, lord of words, one of infinite voice;
truthful in speech, a speaker of truth, and teacher of the Four Truths.
For he is irreversible, a non-returner, a rhinoceros-like solitary leader;
he has emerged through various means of deliverance, and is the single cause of the great elements.
The Arhat, the monk whose taints are exhausted, free from passion, with senses conquered,
has attained security, attained fearlessness, become cooled, and is indeed undisturbed.
Endowed with wisdom and conduct, the Sugata, the supreme knower of the world,
free from "mine-ness" and free from egoism, abides in the method of the two truths.
Standing at the far shore of saṃsāra, having accomplished what was to be done, he stands firm on dry land;
he is one who has emerged through the knowledge of absolute liberation, whose weapon is wisdom, and who rends [all bonds].
The True Dharma is the radiant King of Dharma, the supreme illuminator of the world;
it is the Lord of Dharma, the King of Dharma, and the teacher of the path to the highest good.
He whose purpose is accomplished and whose resolve is fulfilled is free from all conceptual constructions;
he is the non-conceptual, inexhaustible realm, the supreme and imperishable *dharmadhātu*.
Possessing merit, he is the accumulation of merit; possessing knowledge, he is the great source of knowledge;
possessing wisdom, he is the knower of the real and the unreal, fully endowed with the two accumulations.
He is eternal, the sovereign of the universe, the yogi, meditation, the object of meditation, and the lord of the intellects;
he is to be personally realized within, immovable, the supreme primordial one, and the sustainer of the three bodies.
The Buddha is the nature of the five bodies, the pervasive lord whose nature is the five wisdoms;
he wears a crown consisting of the five Buddhas and possesses the five eyes that hold all without attachment.
The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme and most excellent son of the Buddha,
he is the source from whom wisdom arises, the womb of phenomena, and the bringer of an end to cyclic existence.
He is the solid, singular essence, of the nature of a vajra; he is Sadyojāta, the Lord of the World;
born from space, the self-existent one, the great fire of the wisdom of insight.
Vairocana, the great radiance; Virocana, the light of gnosis; the lamp of the world; the torch of gnosis; the one of great splendor; the luminous one.
King of Vidyās, supreme lord of mantras, king of mantras who accomplishes the great purpose;
Great Uṣṇīṣa, wondrous Uṣṇīṣa, beholder of all, lord of the sky.
The foremost embodiment of all Buddhas, whose eyes bring joy to the world,
he who possesses universal form, the creator, the one worthy of worship and honor, the great seer.
The mantra-practitioner upholds the three families, maintains the mantra of the great samaya,
bears the Three Jewels as supreme, and is the teacher of the highest of the three vehicles.
Amoghapāśa, the victorious one; Vajrapāśa, the great seizer;
Vajrāṅkuśa, the great noose; Vajrabhairava, the terrifier.
Thus end the twenty-four and a quarter verses on the Wisdom of the Utterly Pure Dharmadhātu.
The King of Wrath is six-faced and terrifying, with six eyes, six arms, and great strength;
he has formidable fangs, is a skeleton, is Halāhala, and possesses a hundred faces.
Yamāntaka, King of Obstacles, Vajravega, the Terrifier;
Vighuṣṭavajra, Hṛdvajra, Māyāvajra, and Mahodara.
Lord of the thunderbolt, born from the vajra, the vajra-mandala like the sky;
possessing the majesty of a single immovable matted lock, he wears a fresh garment of elephant hide.
The great and terrible cry of "hā hā," the terrifying sound of "hī hī," the loud laughter,
the great laughter, the diamond-like laughter, and the great roar.
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajra King, Great Bliss;
Vajra Fierce One, Great Joy; Vajra Hūṃkāra, the Utterer of Hūṃ.
Wielding the weapon of the vajra-arrow, the vajra-sword that severs;
the bearer of the universal vajra, the Vajrin, the sole Vajrin who destroys the clamor of battle.
His eyes are formidable with vajra-flames; his hair is vajra-flames.
He is the vajra-penetration, the great penetration; he has a hundred eyes and vajra-eyes.
His body consists of hair-tips as hard as vajras; his entire form is composed of vajra-hair;
he has the onset of vajra-pointed nails, and his skin is as dense as the essence of the vajra.
The glorious one who wears a vajra garland, adorned with vajra ornaments;
whose roar is a loud, echoing laugh, the sound of the vajra, and the six-syllable mantra.
Mañjughoṣa, the great roar, the single great sound of the three worlds;
his voice extends to the limits of the realm of space, he is the best among those who possess a voice.
Thus, there are ten verses on the mirror-like wisdom, including this one verse:
Suchness, true selflessness, the limit of reality, and the ineffable;
the bull among those who proclaim emptiness, whose roar is profound and vast.
The great sound of the conch of Dharma, the great drum of Dharma, the great battle-cry;
the drum of Dharma in the ten directions, which is non-abiding nirvana.
Formless yet possessing form, foremost, manifold in form yet mind-made;
the glory that illuminates all forms, he who bears the reflection of everything without exception.
Invincible, of great renown, the Great Lord of the three realms;
established upon the exalted Noble Path, the Banner of Dharma, of vast success.
The body of the sole youth of the three worlds, he is the ancient, aged Lord of Creatures;
bearing the thirty-two marks, he is the beloved, the beauty of the three worlds.
The teacher of the qualities of worldly knowledge, the world-teacher, the fearless one;
the protector, the savior, the friend of the three worlds, the refuge, the supreme deliverer.
Enjoying the vast expanse of space, he is an ocean of omniscient wisdom;
he is the shatterer of the eggshell of ignorance and the destroyer of the cage of existence.
Having pacified all afflictions and crossed to the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra,
he is crowned with the consecration of primordial wisdom and adorned with the ornaments of a perfectly awakened Buddha.
He is the pacifier of the suffering of the three types of suffering, the ender of the three [worlds], the infinite one who has attained the three liberations;
he is completely freed from all obscurations and has reached equality with space.
Transcending the stains of all afflictions, he has reached the state that is beyond the three times;
he is the great elephant among all beings, the crest-jewel upon the crowns of all virtues.
Completely liberated from all limiting adjuncts, he is well-established on the path of space;
the all-pervading Lord, the supreme among all jewels, wears the great wish-fulfilling gem.
He is the vast and flourishing great wish-fulfilling tree, the supreme and great auspicious vase;
he is the performer of the welfare of all beings, the doer of good, the seeker of their benefit, and the one who is affectionate toward sentient beings.
He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the time, he knows the ritual observances, and he is the master who abides by those observances.
He knows the faculties of sentient beings, he knows the proper occasion, and he is skilled in the three types of liberation.
He is possessed of qualities, a knower of qualities, a knower of the Dharma, praised, and the source of auspiciousness;
he is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, renown, fortune, glory, and the auspicious itself.
He is the great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, and the great delight;
he is honor, hospitality, prosperity, joy, glory, and the lord of fame.
The one to be chosen, the giver of boons, the most excellent, the worthy refuge,
the supreme shelter, the enemy of great fear, the most preeminent, the destroyer of every trace of fear.
He has a crest, wears a topknot, has matted hair, possesses locks of hair, is shaven-headed, and wears a diadem;
he is five-faced, has five tufts of hair, and has five rags as his head-ornament.
Wearing the great vows, girded with a muñja-grass belt, a celibate student, the best of those who observe vows,
a great ascetic devoted to austerity, a graduate of the Vedic studies, Gautama is the foremost leader.
The knower of Brahman, the Brāhmaṇa, Brahmā—having attained the nirvāṇa of Brahman;
liberation, release, the limb of liberation, emancipation, tranquility, and auspiciousness.
Nirvāṇa, cessation, peace, the supreme good, the exit, the end;
it is the maker of an end to pleasure and pain, the finality, dispassion, and the exhaustion of the limiting adjuncts.
Unconquered, incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance, and stainless;
partless, all-pervading, omnipresent, subtle, the seed, and untainted.
Free from dust, stainless, immaculate, with faults cast out and free from affliction;
perfectly awakened, the self-awakened one, the supreme knower of all and the all-knowing.
Transcending the nature of consciousness, he bears the form of non-dual gnosis;
free from conceptual construction and effortless, he performs the deeds of the Buddhas of the three times.
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha, free from causal succession;
he is the stainless single eye of gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata.
Lord of Speech, great debater, king of speakers, bull among disputants,
the best of those who speak, most excellent, lion of speakers, unconquered.
Samantadarśin, Pramodita, Tejomālin, Sudarśana, Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dīpti, Bhā, and Bhāsurakaradyuti.
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of thorns;
the tree of all medicines without exception, he is the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions.
The beloved ornament of the three worlds, glorious, a mandala of stars,
extending to the limits of the sky in the ten directions, he is the great, lofty banner of Dharma.
The sole vast umbrella of the world, the mandala of loving-kindness and compassion,
the glorious Padmanṛtyeśvara, the great sovereign Ratnacchatra.
The great king of all buddhas, who sustains the embodiment of all buddhas;
the great yoga of all buddhas, the sole teaching of all buddhas.
The glory of the vajra-jewel initiation, the sovereign lord of all jewels,
the lord of all lords of the world, the supreme master of all vajra-holders.
The great mind of all Buddhas, the movement of the minds of all Buddhas,
the great body of all Buddhas, and the eloquence of all Buddhas.
The Vajra-Sun, the great illumination; the Vajra-Moon of stainless radiance;
the Great Passion beginning with dispassion; blazing with light of every color.
The Perfectly Awakened One, seated in the vajra posture, who upholds the Dharma of the Buddhas' assembly;
the glorious one born from the lotus of the Buddhas, who holds the treasury of omniscient wisdom.
The king who wields the universal illusion, the great master of the vidyās of the Buddhas;
the sharp vajra, the great sword, pure and the supreme syllable.
He who wields the great weapon of the Vajra-Dharma, the Mahāyāna that severs suffering;
Jinajik, profound as a vajra, possessing vajra-intelligence, and knowing things as they truly are.
The fulfiller of all perfections, the ornament of all stages,
possessing the purity of the selflessness of phenomena, with the light of perfect wisdom as his heart’s radiance.
The great exertion of the Net of Illusion, the supreme sovereign of all tantras;
he whose vajra posture is complete, who sustains the entire body of gnosis.
Samantabhadra, the one of excellent intelligence, Kṣitigarbha, the sustainer of the world,
the great womb of all Buddhas, and the bearer of the wheel of universal emanations.
The supreme essence of all phenomena, the sun that illuminates the nature of all things;
he whose nature is non-arising, who exists for the sake of the universe, and who is the light that reveals the true nature of all dharmas.
Possessing great wisdom in a single instant, upholding the realization of all phenomena,
he is the direct comprehension of all dharmas, the Sage who has reached the limit of reality, endowed with supreme intelligence.
Stable, with a perfectly serene mind, he upholds the awakening of the Truly Perfect Buddha;
he is manifest before all Buddhas, a flame of wisdom, most brilliantly radiant.
Thus end the forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment:
The supreme accomplisher of desired aims, the purifier of all lower realms,
the protector most excellent among all beings, the liberator of all beings.
The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy ignorance;
he who possesses wisdom, who bears the erotic sentiment, the glorious one, assuming both heroic and loathsome forms.
He casts forth hundreds of staff-like arms and dances with the planting of his feet;
he performs a dance across the expanse of the sky with the full extension of his glorious hundred arms.
He stands with the sole of one foot treading upon the surface of the earth's mandala,
while his big toe and nail tread upon the summit of the cosmic egg.
The single meaning is the meaning of non-dual phenomena; it is the ultimate reality, indestructible.
The meaning of various representations and forms is the continuum of mind and consciousness.
Delighting in the meaning of all phenomena without exception, he delights in emptiness and possesses supreme wisdom;
transcending passion for existence and the like, he finds great delight in the three realms of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud, with the beautiful luster of the autumn moon’s rays;
possessing the brilliance of the orb of the rising sun, and the radiance of great red-colored nails.
With a sublime crest like the peak of a sapphire, bearing hair as dark as a great blue gem,
possessing the splendor of the radiance of a great jewel, he is adorned with the nirvāṇa of the Buddhas.
He causes a hundred world-systems to tremble; he possesses the great stride of the bases of miraculous power.
He is the bearer of great mindfulness, the reality itself, and the sovereign of the fourfold mindfulness and meditative concentration.
He is the fragrance of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, an ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas;
he knows the method of the eightfold path and knows the path of the perfectly awakened ones.
He has great attachment for all sentient beings, yet he is free from attachment, like the sky;
he is born from the minds of all sentient beings and possesses the speed of the minds of all sentient beings.
He knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings; he captivates the minds of all sentient beings;
he knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates; he maintains the purity of the five aggregates.
Abiding at the pinnacle of all deliverance, skilled in all means of deliverance;
established on the path of all deliverance, the teacher of all deliverance.
He has uprooted existence through its twelve links; he maintains the purity of the twelve aspects;
he possesses the form of the method of the four truths; and he maintains the realization of the eight knowledges.
He whose object is the truth in twelve aspects, who knows reality in sixteen aspects,
whose awakening consists of twenty aspects— he is the fully awakened one, the supreme omniscient one.
He manifests millions of emanation bodies of immeasurable Buddhas;
he is the realization of all moments and the knower of the meaning of every moment of mind.
He manifests the welfare of the world through the various methods and means of the diverse vehicles;
having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle.
His self is purified of the realm of afflictions; he brings about the exhaustion of the realm of karma;
he has crossed over the ocean of the floods and emerged from the wilderness of yoga.
He has thoroughly abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and all defilements along with their latent tendencies;
through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion, he unfailingly accomplishes the welfare of the world.
He is the one for whom all perceptions have been abandoned, whose purpose is consciousness, who effects cessation;
he is the object of the minds of all sentient beings and the movement of the minds of all sentient beings.
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings, he has attained equality with their minds;
he gladdens the minds of all sentient beings and brings joy to the minds of all sentient beings.
The established doctrine is free from delusion, devoid of all error;
it possesses a mind beyond doubt, has three purposes, encompasses all purposes, and consists of the three qualities.
The meaning of the five aggregates, existing in the three times, he who manifests every moment,
perfectly awakened in a single instant, and the bearer of the essential nature of all Buddhas.
Bodyless body, supreme body, the one who manifests the pinnacle of bodies;
he who displays all forms without exception, the Jewel Banner, the Great Gem.
Thus, through the suchness of the knowledge of equality, there are twenty-four [deities].
He is to be realized by all the perfectly awakened ones; he is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddha.
He is without syllables, the source of mantras, and the great threefold family of mantras.
The great bindu, which gives rise to the meaning of all mantras, is without syllables;
it is the five-syllabled great void, the bindu-void, and the six-syllabled.
Possessing all forms yet formless, holding the sixteen, the eight, and the four drops;
partless and beyond calculation, he holds the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
Mastering all meditative concentrations and supernormal powers, he knows the lineages and clans of the families of samādhi;
his body is composed of samādhi, the foremost of bodies, the sovereign of all saṃbhogakāyas.
The Nirmāṇakāya is the foremost of bodies, sustaining the lineage of the Buddha’s emanations;
manifesting in all forms throughout the ten directions, it accomplishes the welfare of the world as is appropriate.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods, the lord of the *suras*, the sovereign of the *dānavas*,
the lord of the immortals, the preceptor of the gods, the destroyer, and the lord of the destroyers.
He has crossed the wilderness of existence; he is the sole Teacher, the Guru of the World, renowned throughout the ten directions, and the great Lord of the Gift of Dharma.
Girt with the armor of loving-kindness, clad in the mail of compassion,
and armed with the sword, bow, and arrows of wisdom, he abandons the battle against afflictions and ignorance.
The enemy of Māra, the conqueror of Māra, the hero who brings an end to the fear of the four Māras,
the victor over all the hosts of Māra, the perfectly awakened one, the leader of the world.
He is to be saluted, worshipped, and greeted; he is to be honored constantly;
he is most worthy of adoration, venerable, and the supreme teacher to whom one should bow.
He whose stride traverses the three worlds alone, whose prowess extends to the limits of space,
who possesses the three knowledges, who is learned in the Vedas, who is purified, who possesses the six superknowledges, and who possesses the six recollections.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has transcended the world and possesses great supernatural power;
established in the perfection of wisdom, he has attained the true nature of wisdom.
He knows himself and knows others; he is all, possessed of valor, the foremost of persons.
Having transcended all comparison, he is to be known as the supreme Lord of Wisdom.
The lord of the gift of Dharma is supreme, the teacher of the meaning of the four mudrās; he is most worthy of being attended upon by all beings who proceed toward the three vehicles of liberation.
The supreme glory purified in the ultimate sense, the great one who brings fortune to the three worlds,
the auspicious Mañjuśrī, the bestower of all prosperity, the most excellent among the glorious.
Thus end the fifteen verses on the knowledge of performing what is to be done.
Homage to you, O supreme bestower of boons, O Vajra; homage be to you, O limit of reality! Homage to you, O womb of emptiness, O awakening of the Buddhas; homage be to you!
O passion for the Buddha, homage be to you; O desire for the Buddha, homage again and again.
O joy in the Buddha, homage to you; O delight in the Buddha, homage again and again.
Homage to you, the Buddha’s smile; homage again and again to the Buddha’s laughter.
Homage to you, the Buddha’s speech; homage again and again to the Buddha’s nature.
Homage to you, the source of non-becoming; homage to you, the source of the Buddha.
Homage to you, the source of space; homage to you, the source of primordial wisdom.
Homage to you, O Net of Illusion! Homage to you, the Buddha’s drama!
Homage to you who are all-in-all! Homage be to you, O Body of Gnosis! [...

This is the unique, perfectly pure Litany of Names and Praise of Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva—the embodiment of gnosis of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, the Holder of the Vajra, the Body of Gnosis of all Tathāgatas—which brings about unsurpassed joy, a palace of delight, and great exultation.
For the sake of the complete purification of the secrets of body, speech, and mind;
for the sake of the complete fulfillment and purification of the accumulations of merit and wisdom on the stages that were previously incomplete and unpurified;
and for the sake of attaining the unsurpassed goal not yet attained.
It has been taught and fully revealed by me for the sake of attaining what has not yet been attained, and for the purpose of upholding the guiding principle of all the dharmas of all the Tathāgatas.
"O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this has been revealed, analyzed, made manifest, and empowered by me through the empowerment of the dharmatā of all mantras within your mind-stream."
Thus ends this praise of the first wheel, consisting of eleven words [...].
Then the glorious Vajradhara, joyful and satisfied, with palms joined in reverence,
bowed down to the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
Together with many other lords, the Indras of Secrets who hold the vajra in their hands, and the kings of wrath, he spoke these words aloud: *mans_2*
We rejoice, O Protector; excellent, excellent is this well-spoken word!
A great benefit has been bestowed upon us, which leads to the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
And for the world, which is without a protector and desires the fruit of liberation,
this pure path to excellence has been proclaimed through the method of the Net of Illusion.
Profound, vast, and extensive, of great significance, and accomplishing the welfare of the world—
this is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One.

Thus end the five summary verses. The *Nāmasaṃgīti* of the Blessed Lord Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, the non-dual ultimate reality, spoken by the Blessed Lord Śrī Śākyamuni from the chapter on the Net of Samādhis included within the sixteen-thousand-verse *Ārya-māyājāla* Mahāyoga Tantra, is hereby completed.
